Kynegos diverted a smile to Sofia. It wasn’t a bad smile at all -  but very aware of its effect - and treated her gently. “Your birthday.” He kissed her forehead. “When did it come?”
“Father is a knight, you know?” Perikly helped him from the desk. “Sofia is to have a cat custom-crafted for her in honor of her birthday. She is the daughter of Athens.” Perikly didn’t wink, but he looked like he was squeezing his buttocks to be sure it made a properly-sounding noise.

Perikly enlightened the Princess Sofia on their plans as they pushed through the corridors, Sofia’s expensive dress and expensive shoes having difficulty navigating the maze of thrones, banquet tables, and trophies that were the hallways of the Royal Palace. The volumes, instruments, and furniture between the doors had all been piled up like kindling, their surfaces bristling with burning brands. The well-trained servants hurried among themselves, moving the flapping items near the chimney so that their blushing folds would not catch fire and dance with their naked skin. Ants were arriving to man the extinguishers that stood nearby, perched upon small stools of carved ivory.

The future did not always bring forth a lasting change. If they told the man what he longed to know, he would do these things to the detriment of the whole and they would be at fault for telling. If they told him what they wanted him to hear, he would be offended and none of this would be resolved.
So the king of trees continued to fountain-water then sleep, and the smallest sap-ling chimed in with a melody, and everyone in the valley was lulled into a long slumber — until an oak discovered and alarmed them: a virile tree of the same species was on its way, and it soon enveloped the king entirely in his enormous shaded presence.
